clue.text: Become very interested in following a performer

indicators.note: the keen word comes after the performer's word in the answer

parts.note: a turn is a variety act or performer on a bill
to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: A fan suddenly develops a passion for following a particular entertainer around.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn into something is to change and end up as it, a phrasal synonym for become.

clue.text: Everyone supporting leader of Tories? That's not credible

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece supporting another sits beneath it
the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Tories

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: A sceptic scoffs at the claim that the whole public backs the Conservative leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story or tall tale is an exaggerated, unbelievable one, so tall means hard to credit.

clue.text: Slop urine around, leading to sense of disgust

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of slop urine are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone splashing urine about produces a feeling of revulsion in onlookers.
explanation.definitionFit: Repulsion is strong aversion or loathing, the feeling of being repelled.

clue.text: "Marine creature" misrepresented hen and dormice

indicators.note: calling a hen and dormice a marine creature misrepresents them, and their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has falsely labelled a hen and some dormice as sea animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Echinoderms are sea animals such as starfish and sea urchins, a phylum found only in the ocean.

clue.text: Fashion overlooking nothing about Latin lifestyle

indicators.note: the shortened fashion word wraps around the Latin abbreviation
overlooking means leaving out, so the zero letter is dropped

parts.note: couture is high fashion
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A fashion world indifferent to everything except a Latin way of living.
explanation.walkthrough: COUTURE without its O gives CUTURE, which goes about L.
explanation.definitionFit: Culture is the way of life, customs and habits of a people, close to lifestyle.

clue.text: Anger: popular part of play has start delayed

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the opening letter of the play part is held back and comes later in the word

parts.note: a scene is a division of a play

explanation.surface: Anger in the audience because a crowd-pleasing section of a show began late.
explanation.walkthrough: Delaying the S of SCENE gives CENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense is to make someone furious; as a verb it means to enrage.

clue.text: Finished with stage event? It's more than one can take

definitions.text: It's more than one can take

parts.note: over means ended or finished
a production is a staging of a play or show

explanation.surface: Done with a theatre show that proved too much to handle.
explanation.definitionFit: Overproduction is making more goods than the market can absorb, more than buyers can take.

clue.text: French are monopolising fashion in boyswear

indicators.note: the French verb takes up and holds the fashion word inside it

parts.note: es is the French for are, as in tu es
ton is fashion or style, as in bon ton

explanation.surface: The French dominate the market in clothes for boys.
explanation.definitionFit: Etons are the short jackets and broad collars of Eton College uniform, worn by schoolboys.

clue.text: I'm upset over some Olympic events — errors in programme?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second
upset in a down clue turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: I'm gives the letters IM
sprints are races such as the 100 metres

explanation.surface: An athlete is distressed about some Olympic races, perhaps mistakes in the printed schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Misprints are typographical mistakes, the kind found in a printed programme.

clue.text: Most of novel by French writer, avoiding the sea, heading off for imaginary territory

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter

parts.note: novel means new
Jules Verne was a French novelist

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter

parts.note: travelling overland means going by land, not by sea

explanation.surface: A book by a French author, describing an inland journey to a fantasy land.
explanation.walkthrough: NE (NEW cut short) plus VERNE plus VERLAND (OVERLAND without its head).
explanation.definitionFit: Never Never Land is Peter Pan's fantasy island, a byword for an ideal, unreal place.

clue.text: Decline energy drinks at the outset

indicators.note: at the outset moves the word for drinks to the front, ahead of the energy symbol

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
laps means drinks, as a cat laps milk

explanation.surface: A warning that energy drinks cause a slump right from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the outset' brings LAPS to the start, so E follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip gradually into a worse state, as standards may, is to decline or fall away.

clue.text: Promiscuous champion probing cryptic clues

indicators.note: the champion goes into the jumbled letters as a probe goes in
cryptic means puzzling, so the letters of clues are jumbled

parts.note: a hero is a champion

explanation.surface: A crossword champion investigating puzzles of a racy nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic clues' reads as the crossword's own phrase; here cryptic is the signal to shuffle the word clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Lecherous means given to lust and sexual excess, close to promiscuous.

clue.text: Squander progress after one's swallowed gin

parts.note: to blue money is old slang for spending it recklessly

indicators.note: the run word takes the numeral inside it

parts.note: to run is to make progress
one has, giving the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A drinker wastes their gains after downing some gin.
explanation.walkthrough: BLUE is British slang (also spelt blew) for squandering money; RUN takes in I.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue ruin is old British slang for cheap, poor-quality gin.

clue.text: Problem contributor to blog — time to be banned?

indicators.note: banning the letter removes it from the word

parts.note: a poster is someone who posts on a blog or forum

explanation.surface: A troublesome blog commenter whom moderators may finally exclude.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling question or tricky dilemma.

clue.text: Liberal avoiding lack of communication about source of certain knowledge

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the first letter of certain
avoiding means the Liberal letter is left out

parts.note: silence is the absence of speech

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter, here of certain

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician dodges a communication blackout about where some sure knowledge comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: SILENCE without L is SIENCE, which wraps around C.
explanation.definitionFit: Science originally meant knowledge in general, from Latin scientia.

clue.text: Small agitated flusters indicative of pressure

indicators.note: agitated means shaken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Minor nervous fluttery moments show that someone is under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressful describes a situation causing tension and strain, showing pressure on someone.

clue.text: Conference's last item for discussion provokes strong feeling

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the conference word

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put to a meeting for debate

explanation.surface: The final debate at a party conference stirs up passions.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion is a strong mental feeling such as joy, anger or fear.

clue.text: Becomes liable to Independent regarding attack

parts.note: to incur a penalty is to become liable to it
on means about or regarding

explanation.surface: A politician risks a penalty over the Independent newspaper's coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: An incursion is a sudden raid or invasion into enemy territory.

clue.text: Quickly explain spill

definitions.meaning: to overflow, as a full bath does

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests hastily accounting for a mess; the phrase has two unrelated senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to recap briefly and to overflow a container's brim.

clue.text: Painter, artist bound to rise, capturing origin of humanity

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

indicators.note: the artist and rising bound together hold the first letter of humanity inside them
in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the bound word runs backwards

parts.note: a bound is a leap

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter, here of humanity

explanation.surface: An artist, destined for success, captures what humanity first sprang from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter, artist' looks like two definitions of one man; only Painter defines, and the artist is the RA of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael was the Italian High Renaissance master who painted the School of Athens.

clue.text: Dismisses heads securing entry to university

indicators.note: the heads word holds the university letter firmly inside

parts.note: bonce is British slang for a head

indicators.note: entry to a word is its first letter, here of university

explanation.surface: Head teachers fix a place for a student at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To bounce someone is informal for throwing them out, as a bouncer ejects people.

clue.text: Batches in bread box mostly

parts.note: a bun is a small bread roll

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: a chest is a large box

explanation.surface: Loaves of bread kept for the most part in a bread bin.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunches are groups or collections of things, like batches.

clue.text: Serious gloomy American disposing of millions

indicators.note: disposing of the letter removes it

parts.note: somber is the American spelling of sombre, gloomy
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A grave, melancholy American gives away a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Sober can mean grave and solemn in manner, a synonym for serious.

clue.text: Poet on love and what follows death

indicators.note: in a down clue, the poet sits on the love letter, above it

parts.note: a bard is a poet
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A poet writes about love and the afterlife.
explanation.walkthrough: Bardo is the Tibetan Buddhist intermediate state between death and rebirth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Tibetan Buddhism the bardo is the transitional state a soul passes through after dying.

clue.text: Pressure point, having ignored initial opening

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: ignoring the initial drops the first letter

parts.note: a juncture is a point in time

explanation.surface: A pressure point in acupuncture, used without first making a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressure point' reads as one thing; split it into P and the point word.
explanation.definitionFit: A puncture is a small hole, an opening made by piercing.

clue.text: About to probe Australia, turning up nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the letters upwards, so backwards
the about word goes inside the country word

parts.note: Oz is informal for Australia
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A survey team about to explore Australia finds nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Oz is the informal name for Australia; in a down answer turning up means read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero is the number nought, meaning none at all.

clue.text: Irish county farmer mostly exercised horse with Henry

indicators.note: with means the Henry letter comes alongside
exercised means worked hard, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: a nag is a horse
H is the symbol for the henry, unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A farmer in Ireland worked out a horse along with a man called Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: FARME rearranged gives FERMA. Fermanagh is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Fermanagh is a county in the province of Ulster, part of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Old French city still to be experienced?

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A historic city in France you have yet to visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put on ice is held in reserve for later, so it is still to come.

clue.text: Silly sod going wild, enthralled by officer's shipping news

indicators.note: held captive inside, so the jumbled letters sit within the officer abbreviation

parts.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

indicators.note: going wild means the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A foolish fellow running amok is captivated by an officer's naval bulletin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lloyd's List is a long-running London publication of maritime and shipping intelligence.

clue.text: See 1
